$comment: The source of sf-avatar's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/avatar (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

size.summary: The avatar's size on the ladder: 1/4 and 1/3 for a mark beside small text, 1 the default, 2 and 3 for a profile. On a desktop 20 / 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 56 px for 1/4 to 3; in a compact region (data-sf-density="compact") every step moves one down the avatar's ladder, 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 40 / 48; the phone ladder is 20 / 20 / 28 / 36 / 44 / 52.

line.summary: Takes the text line of this form size instead of a control height, for an avatar beside a label in a row or a table cell.

shape.summary: circle (the default) for a person, square for a company, a group or a project.

image-url.summary: The picture's address. Empty: the initials of text (or of heading), else the placeholder glyph (icon, person by default).

image-alt.summary: The picture's alternative text, when the picture says something the visible name does not.

no-wrap.summary: Keeps heading and description on one line each in the label and card templates, cut with an ellipsis when the place is narrower.

text.summary: The initials drawn when there is no picture; empty takes them from heading.

icon.summary: The placeholder's glyph (a Material Symbols name) for a bot, a system or a service: shown when there is no picture and no text, in place of the initials of the name, which still names the avatar. Empty: the initials of the name, else person. Drawn on the neutral plate, as the person glyph is.

hue.summary: The hue of the static palette the initials are drawn in (owner decision C17): the plate is the hue's container, the ink its on-container. Empty: the neutral look. auto: one of eight hues (pink, amber, lime, green, teal, sky, indigo, purple) picked from the name (heading, else aria-label, else text) by a fixed hash, the same in every browser and on a server; no name, the neutral look. Only initials take a hue: an image and the placeholder stay as they are. The card template without a photo draws the initials on the hue too, auto when hue is empty (owner decision C124). --sf-avatar-background-color and --sf-avatar-color still win.

expressive.summary: The decorative level (owner decision C91, level 2): initials with a hue on an avatar of 64 px or more (C65: covers only on placeholders from 64) stand on a cover of that hue -- the plate stepping into a second container step towards the far corner -- under the same ink. The size ladder ends at size 3 (56 px), so its avatars stay flat; an avatar sized to 64 px or more takes the cover. A photo, the placeholder and the neutral look stay flat. Off by default; data-sf-style="expressive" on the root or a container turns it on for every avatar under it, data-sf-style="strict" turns it off again.

tone.summary: The former name of hue, until 2027-01-01: read when hue is empty, rose as pink and violet as purple (the tones of initials are the static hues of their names since C17). Write hue.

status.summary: A mark at the corner: online, offline, the company badge or the verified badge; none draws nothing. Online and offline join the accessible name in the page's language («в сети», «не в сети»).

heading.summary: The person's name: printed in the label and card templates, the source of the initials, and the avatar's accessible name when aria-label is not given.

description.summary: The line under the name in the label and card templates: a role, a team.

meta.summary: A short fact in the card template, such as a city, with meta-icon before it.

meta-icon.summary: The glyph before meta in the card template (a Material Symbols name).

card-variant.summary: The card template's picture: square (the default) or portrait, a tall picture over the text.

disabled.summary: Draws the avatar unavailable and, where it is a button, makes it inert.

badge-count.summary: A count on the avatar (simai/ui-source#12): a whole number above 0 shows, 0 or empty hides the badge. Above badge-cap it reads «<cap>+»; the exact number joins the avatar's accessible name («Анна Белова, 3 непрочитанных») and the badge's tooltip. On an anchor of size 1/3 or 1/2 a count is drawn as a dot.

badge-dot.summary: A dot on the avatar, a count with no number: something new. Shown when badge-count is not set; with a count, the count is drawn as a dot. Its text equivalent («есть новое» / «new» by default, badge-label to change it) joins the accessible name.

badge-cap.summary: The largest count drawn as a number; a larger one reads «<cap>+».

badge-label.summary: The words the badge adds to the accessible name and its tooltip, in place of the page language's default: for a dot the whole text equivalent; for a count the phrase in plural forms separated by «|» (one|few|many in Russian, one|other in English) with {count} where the number goes.

relations.name: cl-icon
$comment: The placeholder's glyph is an sf-icon element, so its name reaches the icon font request (avatar study AV-8).

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

label.$comment: The avatar beside a heading and a description, the Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form).

card.$comment: The avatar on a card with a heading, a description and a meta line, the Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form).

accessibility.$comment: The avatar is a native button (every template draws one), named by the host's aria-label, else its heading, else its text, else «Аватар» / "Avatar", with the presence word (online, offline) and the badge phrase after it.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-avatar for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: stays a host attribute, read by the base (§3.1, §4.8); no shim
title is a property of every element (§3.1); the shim maps the attribute, the browser keeps its title property

x-summary: Shows a person or organisation as a photo or initials, with an optional availability or verification mark. The default and label templates render a native button whose aria-label names its action; the card template is static and adds a title, description and meta line.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label: a host attribute, read by the base, never a setting (§3.1)
settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
x-decisions: a11y-role: button -- every template draws the avatar as a native button (Enter and Space press it, Tab reaches it). The name is the host's aria-label, the language file's runtime aria-label («Аватар», "Avatar") when unset, with the badge phrase after it (§4.8); the label and card templates print the heading beside it.

title -> heading: title is a property of every element (§3.1, §16 item 26), so the setting is heading and title its dated setting alias (aliases.json, until 2026-12-01). The browser's own title property is left alone (the component no longer overrides it); the attribute still maps. Initials fall back to the heading.
version 1.1.0: a renamed member behind a dated alias is a minor (§4.10, §16.20).
words: the default name is runtime aria-label of the language files, read with sfWord; AVATAR_TEXT is gone. The element keeps answering el.ariaLabel with that word, as it did.
templates: default, label and card name their Lit templates in JavaScript, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles them (a copy nothing draws would drift).
badge-cap is a number with min 1; badge-count stays a string capped by badge-cap.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (the label template: AZ, Анна Захарова, online, size 2) plus an image, initials from the heading, the card, a count badge, verified and disabled.
css-variables: the public variables of src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json the class sheet already reads (§6): five, seven since 1.3.1.

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.2.0: the tone setting and the classes sf-avatar--tone-<name> (UI Chat, owner decision q-4f91278cc7: people recognise conversations by avatars, and initials were all grey). Eight hues of their own in tokens.colour 1.1.0, because the status ramps speak about the world and primary, secondary and tertiary move with a theme's colour. auto hashes the name, not the two letters (js/tone.mjs, docs/docs.md). The default look is unchanged.

version 1.2.2: initials follow the one rule of helpers/text.js (smart helpers 1.0.4; reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 10): one hyphenated name reads as its parts («Жан-Поль» → ЖП) and a letter with a combining accent keeps it. An empty name still draws the placeholder.

version 1.2.3: the company and verified badge drawings take their inks from the colour roles (owner decision C18, 2026-11-08): the plates and glyphs are classes the class sheet paints (component.avatars 1.2.0) -- company --sf-error with --sf-on-error (was a raw red and a raw near-white), verified --sf-primary with --sf-on-primary. Light theme: the verified badge is unchanged (primary-40, white), the company plate is the error role's tone 40, a little darker than the raw red it replaces. Dark theme: both follow their roles (tone 80 plates, tone 20 glyphs) instead of one fixed look.

version 1.3.0 (2026-11-09): the hue setting (owner decision C17, 2026-11-08: avatars and charts have no colours of their own). The initials take a hue of the static palette, the class sf-hue-<name>, and the class sheet draws them on the hue's container in its ink (component.avatars 1.3.0): the plate 50 at 12 light and 24 dark (was the tone's 50 at 20 and 32), the ink tone 10 and 90 (was 30 and 85), chroma 60 (was 48) and each hue's own angle. auto keeps eight hues in the old order, so a name keeps its slot: rose is pink, and the former violet (HCT hue 325) is purple, since a former tone moves at most 15 degrees (dispatcher 2026-11-09). tone is the former name of hue until 2027-01-01 (journal attribute-c17-avatar-tone-to-hue, value-c17-avatar-rose-to-pink); the former classes sf-avatar--tone-<name> still draw (class-c17-avatar-tone-to-hue).

version 1.3.1 (2026-11-10): the offline dot is the disabled ink laid over the place colour (C43, avatars 1.3.5), and its two layers are public variables of the avatar sheet, --sf-avatar-offline-background-color and --sf-avatar-offline-overlay (avatars 1.3.6); css-variables lists both. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.3.2 (2026-11-10): a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The hue setting's words name the eight hues of auto as the code picks them: purple, not violet (the former violet is purple, value-c17-avatar-rose-to-pink; tone.mjs has drawn purple since 1.3.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.3.3 (2026-11-12, avatar offline dot): a patch. The offline dot is the place's dim ink, --sf-on-surface-variant, not the disabled ink over the place colour, which was under 3:1 for a status mark (light 3.10 against the page, 2.56 against the avatar; dark plate 2.48 / 1.67); now at least 6.44 / 4.43 on the page, a card and the grey plate in both themes (avatars 1.3.7, journal value-avatar-offline-dot-dim-ink). The two public variables stay: --sf-avatar-offline-background-color defaults to the dim ink, --sf-avatar-offline-overlay to none.

version 1.4.0 (2026-11-12, owner decisions C91 level 2 and C65): the expressive setting draws sf-avatar--expressive; component.avatars 1.4.0 turns initials of size 3 with a hue into a cover of the hue: the C17 plate (--sf-hue-container) with a second container step laid over it towards the far corner, in OKLab, roles only, the ink unchanged. C65 said covers from 64 px; the avatar ladder ends at size 3 (56 px, 52 on a phone), so that is the one size that takes it. Off by default; the theme's data-sf-style="expressive" turns it on without the setting. Nothing else changes.

version 1.4.1 (2026-11-13, C65/C91 acceptance; one number above the unreleased 1.4.0 it joins): a patch. The cover follows the decided C65 rule, placeholders from 64 px (component.avatars 1.4.1): 1.4.0 gave it to size 3 (56 px, 52 on a phone), which is under 64, so the ladder's avatars are flat again under the expressive setting, and an avatar sized to 64 px or more takes the cover. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Same patch, the card without a photo (owner remark R212, defect AP-2 of control/research/2026-11-13-avatar-placeholder.md): template="card" without image-url drew its media box 0 px tall (192 x 0), because the square and portrait ratios were set on the img alone; the media box itself now keeps the ratio (square 1:1, portrait 9:16), so the empty card shows its placeholder fill at full size and a card with a photo stands at its size before the photo loads. The look of the empty media (initials or a glyph) is not part of this patch.

version 1.5.0 (2026-11-13, owner decision C124; research control/research/2026-11-13-avatar-placeholder.md, prototype prototypes/avatar-placeholder.html; one number above the unreleased 1.4.1 it joins): a minor, a look change. The card template without image-url draws its media box instead of an empty grey block: with a name (heading, else aria-label, else text) the initials on the hue of the name -- auto is the card's default when neither hue nor tone is set, a named hue is kept -- in the hue's container and ink, as the round avatar with hue="auto" draws them; with no name the person glyph on the neutral fill (surface-container, on-surface-container-variant), the round placeholder's colours. The initials are 36 % of the media box width in the medium weight, the glyph 45 % of it (container query units, the media exception of C18), centred; the box keeps its ratio (1.4.1), so a photo arriving later shifts nothing. Round avatars unchanged. component.avatars 1.5.0 carries the sheet (.sf-avatar-card-placeholder--text, --icon, .sf-avatar-card-initials). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1 (written on fix/content-precheck as 1.3.3; 2026-11-10, docs precheck smart content AV-01): a patch. With component.avatars 1.4.0 the label group may be narrower than its text, so no-wrap lines end in an ellipsis (the group took the text's whole width, 499 in a 300 frame). Every setting has its summary. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.6.0 (2026-11-14, avatar study defects AV-2, AV-4, AV-5, AV-8; control/research/2026-11-14-avatar.md): a minor. (1) The accessible name is the host's aria-label, else heading, else text, else the language word: heading named nobody (the button read «Аватар»). el.ariaLabel answers as before. (2) Online and offline join the name after it, before the count, in the page's language (lang runtime status-online, status-offline: «в сети», «не в сети»; «online», «offline»). (3) The icon setting: the placeholder's glyph for a bot, a system or a service, drawn when there is no picture and no text in place of the initials of the name (person when empty and nameless); the glyph is an sf-icon element (cl-icon relation) and is asked for before the avatar draws. (4) The picture's classes and content are one drawing, js/picture.js, which sf-avatar-group, sf-tag, sf-list-item, sf-dropdown, sf-input-lookup, sf-menu-context and sf-list's signs draw too; sf-avatar's own markup keeps its utility classes (they stay in js/templates/shared.js, where the template-utilities table reads them), a host's picture writes none and takes the same box from component.avatars 1.8.0 (.sf-avatar--picture, in sf.base), so no host asks the Loader for a utility it did not ask for before. (5) core.styles holds the avatar's box before its code (sf-avatar:not(:defined)): the default template is a circle of its size step from the first frame, the label template the taller of the avatar and its heading and description lines (one text line of the size each). Look unchanged.

$comment-after: The badge sheet places a count or a dot on the avatar

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-avatar when the interface needs the avatar behavior.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

aria-label.description: Empty: the heading, else the text, else the word of the page's language ("Avatar" in English).
